title: Saturday Mistakes Episode 1: 5 Common English Mistakes & How to Fix Them
dek: A full breakdown of 5 common English speaking mistakes from Episode 1 of Saturday Mistakes, with clear rules, structures, examples, and practice quizzes (Segment: 00:00 – 22:18).

blocks.text: Hello, language lovers! Welcome to **CosyLanguages Saturday Mistakes Episode 1**. Every week we look at real student mistakes, understand why they happen, and learn how to avoid them with structured formulas and memory hooks. Today, we break down **5 common English mistakes**.

blocks.text: 1. "I will be go" — Why is BE there?
blocks.say: 1. I will be go — Why is BE there?

blocks.text: Many learners mix two different structures: **will + verb** ("I will go to the cinema") and **will be + verb-ing** ("I will be working at nine"). After *will*, use the basic form of the verb (*will go, will eat, will work*).
blocks.say: Many learners mix two structures. After will, use the basic form of the verb: will go, will eat, will work.

items: 📐 **Structure:** Subject + **will** + [Base Verb] *(Simple Future)* OR Subject + **will be** + [Verb-ing] *(Continuous Future)*
❌ **Incorrect:** *I will be go to the cinema.*
✅ **Correct:** *I will go to the cinema.* or *I will be going to the cinema.*
💡 **COSY Hint:** If you use *be*, the next verb MUST end in *-ing*! Never put *be* directly before a bare verb like *go* or *eat*.
💡 **Your Turn:** Which is correct? A. I will be visit... B. I will visit my parents tomorrow. C. I will visiting... (Answer: **B**)
📌 **COSY Rule of Thumb:** Keep *will + bare verb* and *will be + verb-ing* in separate compartments!
blocks.say: Incorrect: I will be go. Correct: I will go to the cinema. COSY Rule of Thumb: Keep will + verb and will be + verb-ing separate!
2. I spend time for learning English

blocks.text: In English, the natural structure is **spend + time + verb-ing** (e.g. *spend an hour learning English* or *spend two hours cooking*).
blocks.say: In English, the natural structure is spend + time + verb-ing.

items: 📐 **Structure:** Subject + **spend** + [Time / Money] + **[Verb-ing]**
❌ **Incorrect:** *I spend one hour for learning English every day.*
✅ **Correct:** *I spend one hour learning English every day.*
💡 **COSY Hint:** Do not insert 'for' or 'to' after 'spend time'! The gerund (*-ing*) connects directly to the time phrase.
💡 **Your Turn:** Which is correct? A. I spend thirty minutes to read... B. I spend thirty minutes reading before bed. C. I spend thirty minutes for read... (Answer: **B**)
📌 **COSY Rule of Thumb:** When you say *spend time*, jump straight to *-ing*!
blocks.say: Incorrect: I spend one hour for learning English. Correct: I spend one hour learning English. COSY Rule of Thumb: When you see spend time, jump straight to -ing.
3. I have no some problems

blocks.text: You are combining two negative structures (*no + noun* vs *don't + verb + any + noun*). Choose one, not both!
blocks.say: You are combining two negative structures. Choose one structure, not both!

items: 📐 **Option 1:** Subject + **have** + **no** + [Noun] *(I have no questions)*
📐 **Option 2:** Subject + **don't have** + **any** + [Noun] *(I don't have any questions)*
❌ **Incorrect:** *No, I have no some questions.*
✅ **Correct:** *I have no questions.* OR *I don't have any questions.*
💡 **COSY Hint:** *No* and *some* cancel each other out like oil and water. Never pair them together!
💡 **Your Turn:** "I checked my bag, but I have ___ snacks." A. no some B. any C. no (Answer: **C**)
📌 **COSY Rule of Thumb:** Pick *no + noun* OR *don't + verb + any + noun*. Simple!
blocks.say: Incorrect: I have no some questions. Correct: I have no questions or I don't have any questions. COSY Rule of thumb: Choose no + noun OR don't + verb + any + noun.
4. I arrived the station — Preposition Needs

blocks.text: Some verbs require specific prepositions before their object (*arrive at the station*, *listen to music*).
blocks.say: Some verbs require specific prepositions before their object like arrive at the station, or listen to music.

items: 📐 **Structure:** Subject + **arrive at** + [Building / Station / Airport] OR **arrive in** + [City / Country]
❌ **Incorrect:** *Yesterday, I arrived the station at six.* • *I listened music.*
✅ **Correct:** *I arrived at the station at six.* • *I listened to music.*
💡 **COSY Hint:** Arrive *at* for places with walls or boundaries (stations, offices); arrive *in* for cities & countries (Paris, France).
💡 **Your Turn:** Which is correct? A. We discussed about the problem. B. We discussed the problem. C. We listened the problem. (Answer: **B**)
📌 **COSY Rule of Thumb:** Learn verbs with their target prepositions attached: *arrive at*, *listen to*, *discuss* (no about).
blocks.say: Incorrect: I arrived the station. Correct: I arrived at the station. COSY Rule of thumb: Learn verbs with short example phrases.

blocks.text: 5. "It depends of you" — The Preposition Trap
blocks.say: 5. It depends of you — The Preposition Trap

blocks.text: Prepositions in English cannot always be directly translated. Fixed expressions require fixed prepositions (*depend on*, *interested in*, *good at*, *wait for*, *worried about*).
blocks.say: Prepositions in English cannot always be directly translated. Learn fixed combinations.

items: 📐 **Structure:** Subject + **depend on** + [Person / Factor / Situation]
❌ **Incorrect:** *It depends of you.*
✅ **Correct:** *It depends on you.*
💡 **COSY Hint:** Many languages use 'of' or 'from' for dependence, but in English you rest *on* something for support — hence *depend ON*!
💡 **Your Turn:** "I'm interested ___ learning French." A. on B. in C. at (Answer: **B**)
📌 **COSY Rule of Thumb:** Don't memorize single words—memorize pairs like *depend on*, *interested in*, *good at*.
blocks.say: Incorrect: It depends of you. Correct: It depends on you. Answer to quiz: interested in.
Summary and Next Steps

blocks.text: Choose two mistakes from today's episode, write three practice sentences with each structure, and test them in your next conversation! Be sure to check out Part Two for the 5 French mistakes.
